use /lib

export shape TaskTableNoticesShape:
    description:
        A notice is something the application tells the run's reader about
        the run, rather than something the harness did or a failure: chiefly
        that it put back changes a task made where its mode may not change
        anything, a Code task in the spec or a Spec task in the code. It is
        passive. It is never shown as an error, never in the theme's error
        colour, and never fails the task, changes its status, or counts among
        the errors a run ended with.

    row:
        A notice is a row of its own, where it happened among the run's rows,
        its badge reading "Notice" with an info icon, in the muted grey of a
        badge that marks nothing wrong. Its output is a single line summing
        it up, muted, beside a right chevron, such as "Put back 3 spec files
        this Code task changed" or "Put back 1 code file this Spec task
        changed". It has no status.

    details:
        Clicking the line expands the notice's details in place, beneath it,
        and its chevron turns down; clicking it again collapses them. For
        changes put back, the details say that a task in its mode may not
        change that location, so what it changed there was put back as it
        was, and then list each file put back, one per line, by its path in
        the project. A notice starts collapsed, and each stays as it was left
        for as long as the application runs.

    kept:
        A notice is kept with its task, and shown the same wherever the
        task's output is, the latest task's table, a previous task opened,
        and a Freeform or Ask reply read as a chat, where it sits among the
        reply's steps as a muted line that expands the same way, never at
        the reply's end with its errors.
115:    protectedLocations:
    protectedLocations:
        Only a run on the host has protected locations. A run in a container
        has none, since nothing it mustn't touch is mounted there, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says: it isn't guarded, and its harness is
        given no rule against reading or editing anything.

        Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude
        Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its
        mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a
        Spec task the code location; the application puts back what the task
        changed there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a
        passive notice, never an error, as the @{TaskTableScope} says.

        It puts back only what the task itself changed: a file the task's own
        tool calls report writing, editing, moving, or deleting there, a
        subagent's included, as the referenced spec works them out, and
        nothing else. A file changed there while the task runs by anything
        else, the user copying a folder in, the editor saving, git, or
        another program, is the user's and is never put back, deleted, or
        reverted, however it changed. It puts back once, when the task is
        over, never while it runs, so nothing is watched and undone as it
        happens; and where a file the task changed was also changed by
        something else since, it is left as it is, the notice saying so,
        rather than overwriting the other change. A task that isn't running
        guards nothing: no location is guarded while no Code or Spec task
        runs on the host, and nothing the application does ever deletes a
        file the user put in the spec or code location, outside what
        `piton build` writes and owns by its manifest. A Code
        task is also told it may not read the spec location, alongside that,
        so it reads the compiled reference instead, as the
        @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says. A question from the Ask tab always
        runs in a container, so it is never given this rule, nor any other
        telling it to keep off the spec location. This rule is only a nudge, and
        doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the
        files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that
        takes no such rules is told nothing of either.

    feeding:

content.text:
Mostly, no, so I've removed it. Podman already sandboxes Spec tasks, Chain spec steps and questions, which had no guard anyway. The guard only ever applied to Code tasks and Chain code steps, which run on your machine where Podman doesn't reach, and it was what deleted your copied folder. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

- **Nothing is put back:** Suspense never reverts, restores or deletes files a run changed, and never watches a folder to undo changes.
- **Code tasks are only nudged:** they're still told, through `--disallowedTools`, not to edit or read the spec. That isn't enforced.
- **Notice instead:** if a Code task changes spec files anyway, its output shows a passive notice such as "This Code task changed 3 spec files". The files are left as the task left them. The notice lists them, and each opens its diff, so you can keep or undo the change yourself.

**Trade-off:** a Code task that ignores the rule can now change your spec. If you'd rather enforce it, the alternative is running Code tasks in a container too.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `HarnessIntegrationScope` `#protected-locations` (the put-back logic goes), and `TaskTableScope` `#notices`.
